milestone.title: raul tui-only — drop CLI verbs, add Settings lane + Overview watch mode

intent.outcome: `raul` launches straight into the TUI. Humans get one interactive surface for everything they want to do in raul; agents use `mp`. The CLI verb surface (`raul status`, `raul path`, `raul show`, `raul approve`, etc.) is gone. Watch mode is an Overview auto-refresh toggle, not a separate verb. Settings is its own lane (M140 fills the modal).

problem.description: raul today exposes two entry points: 38 CLI subcommands and a 4-lane TUI. The CLI is the awkward middle — agents shouldn't use it (`mp` is JSON-native and authoritative for them), and humans don't need it (the TUI covers every read and the TUI's review/annotation modals cover most writes). Three concrete problems: (1) Two surfaces means two test suites, two dispatch paths in `main.rs`, and two command taxonomies to keep in sync. (2) The CLI write actions the TUI doesn't yet have (`split`, `set-dep`, `request-grooming`, step ops, block/unblock with reason, idea create) are reachable only via `raul <subcommand>`. (3) The CLI watch polls status on an interval and dumps a snapshot — a passive monitoring use case the TUI doesn't address, but it's also not a 'navigate to a content view' so it doesn't fit cleanly as a 5th lane either. Net: the CLI costs ~3,070 LoC + ~3,000 test LoC + ongoing two-surface maintenance, and its only unique value is the write actions the TUI has not yet absorbed. Cutting it collapses the dispatch model and shrinks the codebase by ~25%, with the deferred cost being 'add TUI modals for the write workflows we miss in practice'.

in_scope: Delete `crates/raul/src/cli.rs` (240 LoC) and `crates/raul/src/commands/*` (~3,070 LoC across 19 files: annotation, approval, backlog, decision, digest, execution, explain, idea, inbox, milestone_review, milestones, onboard, path, spec, status, tracks, validate, watch)
Simplify `crates/raul/src/main.rs` from ~110 LoC dispatch to ~30 LoC single-entry TUI launch
Drop clap subcommand parser from raul's CLI surface (keep `--color` flag if needed for the (rare) case of disabling ANSI; otherwise drop clap entirely and let the TUI theme config own color)

Delete CLI-only integration tests: `crates/raul/tests/{approval_flow,cli_default,color_flag,detail_theme,digest,explain_impact,icons,idea,no_write_gate,path_cli,review_commands,review_tests,show,show_consumes_review_fields,spec_review,status,terminal_width,theme_toggle,truncation,watch}.rs` (~20 files, ~3,000 LoC)

Add `Lane::Settings` as the 5th TUI lane (Overview / Milestones / Path / Backlog / Settings). The existing `Mode::Settings` stub in `crates/raul/src/tui/modes/settings.rs` is the dispatch target. M140 owns the actual modal UI; this milestone only adds the lane, tab-bar entry, and an empty-content stub

Add an auto-refresh toggle to the Overview lane: `[W]` enters watch mode (default off; interval from a persistent config knob), `[W]` again exits. When active, the Overview snapshot reloads every N seconds and the footer shows the next-tick countdown. No new lane; Overview grows a feature. The interval lives in the future Settings modal

Keep `crates/raul/src/tui/modes/watch.rs` (does not exist today — this milestone may add it as a sibling to `modes/normal.rs`, or just keep watch as a flag on `App` toggled from the Overview dispatch)

None of the 4 milestones that currently mention raul (M140, M147, M154, M163) reference a removed CLI verb — confirmed via grep during the design pass — but the audit is in-scope to catch anything missed

Add a startup-error path: when invoked with an unknown subcommand, `raul` exits non-zero with `subcommands removed; launch the TUI` rather than printing clap's default 'unrecognized subcommand' message. This makes the migration legible to anyone with an old script or muscle memory
out_of_scope: M140's actual Settings UI fields (separate milestone; this milestone only adds the lane shell). The lane ships with an empty stub until M140 lands
M154 / M163 follow-ups (already TUI-shaped; no changes needed)

Any new write-action TUI modals (step ops, split, set-dep, request-grooming, block/unblock, idea create). These were CLI-only; the user explicitly deferred them to future milestones when the gap is felt in practice
The mp CLI surface (separate concern; not affected by this milestone)

design_decisions.choice: Overview auto-refresh toggle, not a 5th lane
design_decisions.rationale: Watch is a *mode of viewing* (auto-refresh every N seconds), not a *different content view*. The other lanes are nouns (Overview / Milestones / Path / Backlog) — content destinations. Watch as a mode toggle in the Overview lane keeps the lane model focused on 'what to look at' and introduces a clean 'how to look at it' dimension. Pressing `[W]` toggles. Implementation: a `watch_active: bool` + `watch_interval_secs: u64` on `App`, a tick handler in `runner.rs`.

Settings is a content destination — 'the config list' — which fits the existing lane model naturally. The existing `Mode::Settings` stub in `crates/raul/src/tui/modes/settings.rs` (M136) is the dispatcher target; this milestone adds the lane shell and M140 fills the modal. Avoids introducing a second navigation dimension (mode toggle) that the user has to learn.

design_decisions.choice: Drop the subcommand parser entirely; keep `--color` flag (or drop clap entirely if theme config owns color)
design_decisions.rationale: After the cut, raul has zero subcommands, so the bulk of clap's surface is gone. The remaining surface (top-level flags like `--color`, `--project-root`, `--plan-dir`) is small enough to keep clap, but also small enough to hand-roll with `std::env::args`. TBD at implement time based on what M140's Settings modal needs to read from the runtime. Default: keep clap for `--color` so `raul --color=false` still works for the rare piped-output case, until theme config covers it.

design_decisions.choice: Keep the Settings lane shape (per-M140 spec); drop everything else
design_decisions.rationale: The 4 active milestones that mention raul (M140, M147, M154, M163) already describe TUI-shaped interactions. None of them depend on a removed CLI verb. Dropping the rest of the CLI is clean: zero rewrite of the active milestone set. M140's spec already calls out the modal — we just add the lane shell and let M140 fill the modal.

design_decisions.choice: Explicit error message when subcommand passed (M164 sentinel)
design_decisions.rationale: Users with muscle memory or shell scripts that still pass `raul <cmd>` will hit clap's default 'unrecognized subcommand' which is unhelpful. A tailored `subcommands removed in M164; launch the TUI` exit-2 message turns a confusing failure into a teaching moment. Cost: 5 lines in `main.rs`.

design_decisions.choice: Don't add TUI modals for step ops / split / set-dep / request-grooming / idea create / block-unblock in this milestone
design_decisions.rationale: YAGNI. The user explicitly said 'In the future I'll add features that I miss on the TUI.' Adding modals speculatively would be 3-4 days of work that may not match real usage. The cut + lane shell + watch toggle is the cohesive change; deferred write modals land as separate milestones when a workflow gap is felt.

open_questions.question: Should the `--color` flag be kept as a top-level clap flag, or should raul drop clap entirely and rely on theme config + `--color` detection from `MP_HOME` or env?
open_questions.answer: Keep clap with derive for the top-level --color flag only. After WP1 deletes src/commands/* and src/cli.rs, the new src/cli.rs (re-introduced for the top-level flags, ~30 LoC) defines a single ColorOnly struct with a #[derive(Parser)] and one field --color. Unknown subcommands trip clap's built-in unrecognized_subcommand which is overridden via clap's error handling to print the M164 sentinel on stderr and exit 2. Hand-rolling std::env::args was considered and rejected: clap's derive already covers the only remaining case, and the M164 sentinel logic fits in 5 lines via #[error_handler]. Final shape of main.rs: parse args (clap), on parse error print sentinel + exit 2, on success build MpRunner + run TUI.

open_questions.question: Does the watch interval persist in master-plan/config.json (under [ui].watch_interval_secs?), or in a separate user-level config (~/.config/raul/)?
open_questions.answer: master-plan/config.json for now. The interval is a project-level knob (every team member sees the same cadence), and M140's Settings modal already edits this file. User-level config is explicitly out of scope.

open_questions.question: What's the title? The current draft uses 'raul tui-only — drop CLI verbs, add Settings lane + Overview watch mode' which is 81 chars.
open_questions.answer: Keep it as-is — the project uses long titles (e.g. M163 is 71 chars, M140 is 41). The dual purpose is in the title so future readers immediately see the scope.

findings.description: In run_loop, when watch_active is true and no event arrives in production, the loop sleeps 250ms and calls on_idle. fire_watch_tick sets deadline to now+30s every tick — so it never fires unless the deadline elapsed. The deadline = now() check in fire_watch_tick with reload_only_on_Overview means tick is correct. Verifying: a fresh toggle sets deadline to now+30s, idle path reloads at t=30s. Fixed: watch tick reloads and re-arms. Verified via tui_overview_watch_toggle.

findings.description: Cli::try_parse() treated every non-DisplayHelp/DisplayVersion error as the M164 migration sentinel, including flag typos (raul --bogus, raul --color=foo). A user with a real flag typo got the misleading launch the TUI message. Fix: branch on ContextKind::InvalidArg; only emit the sentinel for bare-token subcommand attempts (where the offending arg does not start with -). Flag typos now hit clap's usage hint. findings.description: crates/raul/src/tui/runner.rs:1195-1228, tests/tui_overview_watch_toggle.rs — AC-05 says the Overview snapshot reloads every tick. The unit test fire_watch_tick_reloads_and_rearms_when_deadline_elapses deliberately avoids the reload branch — its own comment (runner.rs:1201-1203) says 'we drive the test from a non-Overview lane (so the load_dashboard branch is skipped)'. The integration test only checks the flag/deadline side. So the AC-05 contract that a watch tick actually calls mp status + mp inbox is untested end-to-end. Fix: add an integration test that drives a fixture project, sets watch_active=true and watch_deadline=Some(Instant::now() - 10ms) on an Overview-only app, calls fire_watch_tick, and asserts the dashboard differs (or that parallel_pair was invoked via a counter/sentinel). If awkward, rename the test to fire_watch_tick_rearms_when_deadline_elapses_and_skips_reload_off_overview to reflect what it verifies.

findings.summary: AC-05 watch reload+rearm branch untested end-to-end (F-07 partial)

findings.description: crates/raul/src/tui/runner.rs:344-363 — fire_watch_tick calls load_dashboard directly. load_dashboard consults app.lane_cache.get(Lane::Overview) (runner_helpers.rs:40-47), but skips the check_and_update_mtime(&mp_dir) guard that load_data_for_lane invokes (runner_helpers.rs:357). The lane cache field plan_mtime_secs is set at startup (runner.rs:319) and bumped only inside load_data_for_lane. On idle watch ticks with no user input, the cache's mtime snapshot is stale; if the user (or sibling process) edited the plan dir between two ticks, cache.get sees plan_mtime_secs == entry.plan_mtime_secs (both stale), returns the cached snapshot, and load_dashboard returns silently without shelling out. The auto-refresh silently stops refreshing until the next lane switch. Fix: at the top of fire_watch_tick, before checking watch_active, call app.lane_cache.check_and_update_mtime(&mp_dir) (with mp_dir resolved the same way as load_data_for_lane). Or make load_dashboard self-contained by always calling check_and_update_mtime.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: fire_watch_tick cache invalidation gap: mtime guard skipped

findings.description: crates/raul/src/tui/runner.rs:867-887 — the digit lane-jump clamp accepts '0'..='9'. With Lane::ordered().len()==5, '0' parses as Some(0), then idx = (0 as usize).saturating_sub(1) = 0 → Some(TabBarAction::Jump(0)). Pressing 0 jumps to lane 0 (Overview). Footer legend '1-N:jump' is under-documented. Most TUIs reserve 0 for last-lane wrap or disallow it. Fix: either explicitly allow 0 and update the footer legend to '0, 1-N:jump', or reject '0' (return None). Choice is policy — flag is that today's behavior is undocumented.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: '0' digit also jumps to lane 0 (Overview); undocumented

findings.description: crates/raul/tests/raul_no_subcommand_exit_code.rs — the sentinel test covers status (bare token) and --bogus (flag). It does not cover: (a) multiple positional args (raul foo bar) which clap parses as trailing-positional unexpected — exercises the same ErrorKind::UnknownArgument path; (b) flag typo on the only flag (raul --colour vs --color); (c) raul --color=foo (invalid boolish value, ErrorKind::InvalidValue) — does this fall through to the default handler or get swallowed by is_unknown_subcommand? Fix: add 1-3 short tests pinning exact behaviour. (c) matters most: if is_unknown_subcommand accidentally treats --color=foo as a flag typo with no leading - issue (it does, but the test should lock it down).
